diagnosis: The authenticated original P6 Mathematics scheme combines parallelogram and rhombus work in the Week 3 periods 2/3 row. Its objective column specifies finding the perimeter and area of a rhombus, while its content column states that learners read and draw both the parallelogram and the rhombus. The existing canonical Lesson 2 outcome, 'Read and draw a parallelogram', is supported by the content column. The original Lesson 2 area explanations, equation and numerical worked examples provide useful mathematical enrichment, but the area calculations do not directly assess the canonical read-and-draw outcome. The repair therefore retains all original numerical worked examples, complete solutions and mathematical equations in the pupil edition, identifies area work as optional enrichment, and replaces the Lesson 2 assessment questions with read-and-draw tasks. Original numerical exercises and their answers remain in teacher-only archives. This is a scope and assessment repair, not a claim that the scheme establishes a separate parallelogram-area learning outcome.

block_updates.text: LESSON 2 — READING AND DRAWING A PARALLELOGRAM
Optional enrichment — Area of a parallelogram. If the base and perpendicular height are measured in centimetres, the area is expressed in square centimetres (cm²).
LESSON 2: Worked Examples — Drawing and Optional Area Enrichment

Example 1: Draw parallelogram ABCD. Use a base AB of 6 cm and an adjacent side AD of 4 cm making an angle of 60° with AB. Make AB parallel to DC and AD parallel to BC. Label all vertices. Explain which opposite sides are parallel.

Exercise 2: (1) Draw a parallelogram and label it PQRS. (2) State two properties of its opposite sides. (3) Draw a parallelogram ABCD with AB horizontal and DC parallel to AB. Label all four vertices. (4) Draw a parallelogram EFGH with EF parallel to HG and EH parallel to FG. (5) In parallelogram ABCD, name the two pairs of opposite parallel sides. (6) Draw a parallelogram with a sloping side. Mark its base and draw a perpendicular height to that base.

Exercise 2 answers for teacher checking: Activity: parallelogram; AB parallel to DC; AD parallel to BC; base 6 units and height 4 units. Questions: (1) valid labelled parallelogram; (2) opposite sides parallel and equal; (3) valid parallelogram ABCD with AB parallel to DC and all vertices labelled; (4) valid parallelogram EFGH with EF parallel to HG and EH parallel to FG; (5) AB and DC; AD and BC; (6) valid sloping parallelogram with the chosen base and a correctly marked perpendicular height.
9. Draw and label a parallelogram ABCD. Show both pairs of parallel opposite sides. 10. Draw a parallelogram PQRS. Mark the base PQ and draw a perpendicular height to PQ.

Answers 7–12: 7. 40 cm. 8. 14 cm. 9. Correctly drawn parallelogram ABCD with AB parallel to DC and AD parallel to BC. 10. Correctly drawn parallelogram PQRS with base PQ and a perpendicular height marked at 90° to PQ. 11. 48 cm. 12. 126 cm².
